# M3 reproduction: full 30-dataset run, shared response, figures

Committed summary of M3's result, mirroring `docs/reproduction-m2.md`'s
structure. Regenerable: `scripts/reproduce.py --all`, `scripts/shared_
response.py`, and `scripts/figures.py` write their full outputs to
`results/` (gitignored); this file is the durable, human-readable record of
what those runs found.

## D0. Free wins: all-30 significance/sign agreement, and M2's exact-tie sign-convention question

**Generated by:** `uv run scripts/reproduce.py --all`, run 2026-09-23 (was
2026-09-17; re-run after `mbhd.labels.CONDITION_FILTER`, which changed `edd_singh`/`hiv_lozupone`/`nash_wong`/`ob_goodrich`'s
sample composition).
**Environment:** Python 3.12.3, pandas 3.0.5, numpy 2.5.3, scipy 1.18.1,
statsmodels 0.15.0, pyyaml 6.0.3 (`results/reproduction_all/provenance.json`).

`ob_zupancic` fails outright (`mbhd.abundance.ZeroReadSampleError`, caught,
not a crash) as already reported in M2 -- 29 of 30 datasets produce a
comparison.

### Significance/sign agreement, not just genus-set match

`docs/reproduction-m2.md`'s appendix reported genus-set agreement (missing
vs. extra genera) for all 30 but did not carry the significance/sign
agreement numbers past the four required subset datasets. Those numbers
were already computed by `_diff_table`/`_summarize` and are pulled here at
near-zero cost, split by tier:

| subset | datasets | significance agree / common | sign agree / both-significant | max q-value diff (both sig.) | max effect-size diff (finite) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Clean 24** (M1 sample-count-reconciled *and* genus-set-exact) | 24 | 2280/2280 | 361/361 | 4.5e-7 | 4.5e-11 |
| **Genus-set-exact 27** (clean 24 + `crc_wang`, `liv_zhang`, `ob_turnbaugh`) | 27 | 2459/2459 | 390/390 | 5.7e-3 | 1.4 |
| **All 29 non-erroring** | 29 | 2666/2719 | 420/420 | 4.1e-2 | 12.8 |

> **Updated 2026-09-21** (was "Clean 18"/"Genus-set-exact 21", 1728/1728,
> 265/265, 2.6e-7 from `ibd_gevers`): `mbhd.labels.SAMPLE_TYPE_FILTER`
> fixed a real bug (non-stool samples were never filtered for `ibd_morgan`/
> `ibd_willing`) -- both datasets now reconcile Table 1 *and* reproduce
> their genus set exactly, joining "Clean." `cdi_youngster` reconciles
> Table 1 (M3 step D1) but is *not* genus-set-exact, so it stays out of
> "Clean" -- 18 + `ibd_morgan` + `ibd_willing` = 20, not 21.

> **Updated 2026-09-23** (was "Clean 20"/"Genus-set-exact 23", 1861/1861,
> 270/270, 2643/2714): `mbhd.labels.CONDITION_FILTER` fixed a real,
> previously-unread `condition:` field in MicrobiomeHD's own upstream
> `dataset_info.yaml` for `edd_singh`, `hiv_lozupone`, `nash_wong`, and
> `ob_goodrich` -- all four now reconcile Table 1 *and* reproduce their
> genus set exactly, joining "Clean" -- 20 + 4 = 24, "Genus-set-exact"
> 23 + 4 = 27. The all-29 row's max q-value diff moved from 4.2e-2 to
> 4.1e-2 as a side effect (the driver changed from `hiv_lozupone`, now
> resolved, to `cdi_youngster`, still open -- see below).

**Two things worth stating plainly, not glossing over:**

- Sign agreement is **420/420 across every dataset that has a published-
  significant genus, all 29 non-erroring datasets included** -- every genus
  both this pipeline and the published table call significant agrees on
  direction, even in datasets whose sample count or genus set does not
  fully reconcile. Direction of effect is the most robust part of this
  reproduction.
- The max q-value diff **rises from ~1e-13 (M2's four-dataset result) to
  4.5e-7 within "Clean 20"**. This is now `ibd_morgan` (previously
  `ibd_gevers` at 2.6e-7, still present in the 20 and still below this new
  max); the diff stays far below the 0.05 significance threshold and every
  significance call still agrees, but it is not pure floating-point noise
  the way the four-dataset result was -- flagged here rather than silently
  re-describing it as "noise" again. Not root-caused for either dataset; a
  plausible mechanism (a near-tied Kruskal-Wallis rank sum interacting with
  `benjamini_hochberg`'s sort) is not yet tested.
- **Genus-set-exact does not imply numerically-exact.** `crc_wang`,
  `liv_zhang`, `ob_turnbaugh` reproduce their genus set exactly (M2 finding)
  but not their sample count (`KNOWN_MISMATCHES`) -- a different set of
  samples feeds the same statistical test, so q-values and effect sizes
  genuinely differ (up to 5.7e-3 and 1.4 respectively) even though every
  significance call for them still agrees with the published one. The
  27-dataset row above is a genus-set-membership result, not a claim that
  all 27 match numerically to floating-point precision.
- The **all-29 row's 4.1e-2 max q-value diff** comes from `cdi_youngster`
  (updated 2026-09-23: previously `hiv_lozupone`, now resolved via
  `CONDITION_FILTER`; `cdi_youngster` is the largest of the remaining
  genus-set-mismatched datasets) --
  every significance call for it still agrees regardless.

### M2's exact-tie question: does the exact-tie sign convention ever arise?

**Yes, but it never matters.** Checked directly (not assumed) across all 29
non-erroring datasets: `control_mean == case_mean` exactly on 11 genus-rows,
across 3 datasets (`cdi_youngster`: 7, `nash_zhu`: 2, `ob_zhu`: 2). Every one
of those 11 tied rows has `q_value == 1.0` -- i.e. it is never anywhere near
significant. `signed_qvalues`'s arbitrary "positive on tie" convention
(`src/mbhd/stats.py`) therefore never changes the sign of a genus that is
ever called significant, in this data. The question is closed: the
convention is empirically inconsequential here, not merely undocumented.

> **Correction, 2026-09-23:** this section originally said "21 genus-rows,
> across 4 datasets (`ibd_willing`: 10 ...)" and was never refreshed after
> `mbhd.labels.SAMPLE_TYPE_FILTER` (2026-09-21) changed
> `ibd_willing`'s own sample composition -- its 10 tied rows were an
> artefact of the pre-fix, non-stool-contaminated sample set and do not
> exist post-fix. Found and corrected while re-checking this number after
> the unrelated `CONDITION_FILTER` change; re-verified
> directly against real data, not carried forward from either prior count.

### Exact-zero q-values, answered early as a byproduct

Checked in the same pass: no reproduced `q_value` is ever exactly `0.0`
across all 29 non-erroring datasets. The published data's "exact `0.0` is
not significant" clause (in the published file-S1, 11 cells are exactly
`0.0`, all in `cdi_youngster`, `ob_zhu` and `nash_zhu`; they are treated as
degenerate, and excluding them is required to reproduce either published
shared-response file) therefore has nothing to apply to on our side -- the
policy question of how to treat exact zeros is moot in practice, not merely
deferred. Re-checked formally as part of the E1-E3 test suite below, since a future change
to `mbhd.stats` could reintroduce this.

## D1. `cdi_youngster`'s sample-count mismatch: RESOLVED

The time-boxed investigation (the one
narrow exception to "document, don't chase") confirmed the lead recorded
since M1: Table 1 counts distinct **patients**, not samples, for this one
longitudinal FMT study. The metadata's own `subject` column collapses the
18 intersected H-labelled samples to exactly 4 distinct subjects and the 27
intersected CDI samples to exactly 19 -- both match Table 1's published
`(4, 19)` exactly. Implemented as `mbhd.labels.SUBJECT_ID_COLUMN`; `cdi_
youngster` is no longer in `KNOWN_MISMATCHES` (12 -> 11 open mismatches).
This does not change M2's actual analysis, which already used all 18 H and 27 CDI *samples* (statistical power comes from samples, not patients); it only concerns matching Table 1's reported count.

## E1-E3. `mbhd.shared_response`: the module and its own tests

`src/mbhd/shared_response.py` moves `disease_of`, `is_significant`,
`shared_response_labels`, and the exclusion/prefix constants out of `tests/
test_supplementary_files.py`
and adds `build_qvalue_matrix`, which assembles this project's own
`differential_abundance` output, across as many datasets as requested, into
the same shape the labelling rule already expects. All 10 of `tests/
test_supplementary_files.py`'s regression tests against the *published*
files still pass unchanged, now importing production code. `tests/
test_shared_response.py` adds synthetic tests for `build_qvalue_matrix`'s
own contract (disjoint genus sets, a hard-failing dataset recorded not
dropped, an unexpected exception still propagating, a shared-folder pair
not double-counting as two diseases) plus the real-data check that closed
D0's zero-q-value question formally.

## E4. The shared-response result, from our own reproduced q-values

**Generated by:** `uv run scripts/shared_response.py`, run 2026-09-23 (was
2026-09-21 -- re-run after `mbhd.labels.CONDITION_FILTER`, which changed `edd_singh`/`hiv_lozupone`/
`nash_wong`/`ob_goodrich`'s sample composition). Four comparisons
(`results/shared_response/*.csv`, gitignored), matching the two-run localization design
fixed before the run:

| comparison | our pool | published pool | common lineages | agree | only ours | only published |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| full-29 vs. Zenodo (no exclusions) | 154 | 146 | 144 | 140 | 10 | 2 |
| full-29 vs. GitHub (3 exclusions, **primary target**) | 152 | 144 | 142 | 138 | 10 | 2 |
| clean-27 vs. Zenodo | 139 | 146 | 139 | 129 | 0 | 7 |
| clean-27 vs. GitHub | 133 | 144 | 133 | 126 | 0 | 11 |

> **Updated 2026-09-23** (was 158/155 our pool, 137/138 agree, clean-23 at
> 128/122 our pool, 106/110 agree): `mbhd.labels.CONDITION_FILTER` shrank
> the reproduced pool for both full-29 rows (our pipeline was calling a few
> extra genera significant in the four now-fixed datasets, purely a
> byproduct of their previously-wrong sample composition) while the
> **agree count on the primary target held exactly at 138/142 (97.2%)** --
> the fix changed *which* genera are in the pool, not the primary-target
> agreement rate. `clean-27`'s `n_only_published` fell (18->7, 22->11)
> because the four newly-"clean" datasets bring real evidence for lineages
> the smaller, stricter clean-23 pool previously had no basis to include.

**This is the headline M3 result: the loop from raw OTU tables to the
paper's non-specific-genera finding closes independently, with real but
bounded disagreement, not a false 100% match and not a breakdown.**
Read plainly:

- On the **primary comparison target** (full-29 vs. GitHub), **138 of 142
  lineages both sources have an opinion on agree (97.2%, unchanged by the
  `CONDITION_FILTER` fix -- up from 93% before the earlier `SAMPLE_TYPE_
  FILTER` fix)** -- a real, substantially-reproduced result.
- **The clean-27 run never proposes a lineage the published pool doesn't
  already have** (`n_only_reproduced = 0` in both clean-27 rows) -- every
  disagreement there is the clean-27 pool being a *subset* of the published
  one (`n_only_published`: 7 and 11, down from 18 and 22 -- the four newly-
  "clean" datasets bring real evidence for lineages the smaller, stricter
  clean-23 pool previously had no basis to include). This is expected and
  mechanical, not a new bug: the clean-27 run still has strictly less
  evidence per genus than the full-29 run, so it can only under-populate
  the pool relative to a 30-dataset-derived published file, never
  over-populate it.
- **The full-29 run does propose lineages the published pool lacks**
  (`n_only_reproduced`: 10 and 10, down from 14 and 13) -- these come from
  datasets whose sample count or genus set does not fully reconcile (the
  `cdi_youngster`/`hiv_noguerajulian`/`ob_zupancic` gap, down from 7+`ob_zupancic` after the
  `CONDITION_FILTER` fix), so a reproduced dataset can call a genus
  significant when the published pipeline, working from different
  underlying sample composition, did not. Each such lineage is traceable
  in `results/shared_response/*.csv`'s `reproduced_label`/`published_label`
  columns, but attributing every one individually is not undertaken here --
  named as a real, bounded limitation, not resolved.
- Only 2 lineages are in the published pool but missing entirely from our
  full-29 reproduction (both variants, unchanged) -- a small, real gap, not
  investigated further at M3's time budget.

No claim beyond this is made: this reproduces the paper's headline finding
at a real, quantified, imperfect agreement level from this project's own
pipeline, closing the loop MicrobiomeHD's authors themselves built once,
independently, for the first time in this project.

## F1-F2. Figures

**Scope, decided (Pablo, 2026-09-17):**
Fig 1a (per-study classifier AUC) is descoped to M4 -- no classifier exists
anywhere in this project yet, and building one properly under M3's own time
budget would quietly become M4's actual content instead of M3's. Fig 3a
(phylogenetic presence/absence track) is out of scope permanently: no
phylogeny is ever built in this project. The four remaining panels are
generated as **equivalent plots from this project's own reproduced
numbers, not pixel-identical to the published images** -- a rough-tolerance
secondary check, never the primary
numeric target (the D0/E4 diff tables are that).

**Generated by:** `uv run scripts/figures.py`, run 2026-09-23 (was
2026-09-21; re-run after the `CONDITION_FILTER` fix). Images: `results/figures/*.png` (gitignored).

- **Fig 1b-equivalent** (`fig1b_significant_genera_per_dataset.png`): 9 of
  29 reproduced datasets show more case-enriched than control-enriched
  significant genera (unchanged by the fix).
- **Fig 2-equivalent** (`fig2_qvalue_matrix.png`): 154 genera reach BH
  q<0.05 in at least one of 29 reproduced datasets (30 attempted; was 158);
  grey cells mark a genus absent from that dataset after filtering, not a
  zero.
- **Fig 3b-equivalent** (`fig3b_overlap_per_dataset.png`): across 19
  datasets with >=1 significant genus (was 20 -- `nash_wong`'s own
  significant-genus count changed with its sample composition and no
  longer clears the >=1 threshold under the full-29/GitHub-exclusion
  pool definition), a mean of 70% of a dataset's own significant genera
  also belong to the cross-disease shared-response pool (full-29 run,
  GitHub-style exclusions applied when defining the pool; was 72%).
- **Fig 3c-equivalent** (`fig3c_abundance_ubiquity.png`): shared-response
  genera (n=55, unchanged) have median relative abundance 3.76e-03 (was
  3.91e-03) vs. disease-specific genera (n=99, was 103) at 5.56e-04 (was
  5.27e-04) -- roughly an order of magnitude higher either way, the same
  qualitative direction as the paper's own Fig 3c. Median cross-study
  ubiquity 76% (shared) vs. 31% (specific), unchanged. **Caveat stated
  plainly, not glossed over:** "ubiquity" here is the fraction of this
  project's own reproduced datasets a genus survives study-level filtering
  in -- a cross-study proxy for the paper's own within-study sample
  prevalence, not a reproduction of that exact statistic.

Each figure's axis labels carry units (q-value significance threshold,
relative-abundance scale, fraction), and each caption above states a
concrete, checkable conclusion rather than restating the axes (this project's
plotting rule).
